questions.title: Switching off G protein signalling
questions.question: In G protein coupled receptors the G protein action is switched off by which one of the following specific biochemical processes?

options.A: The extremely fast direct total activation of the target functional protein
options.B: The completely full alpha subunit totally replacement of GDP for GTP
options.C: The extremely rapid total dissociation of the beta and delta subunits from alpha

explanations.A: Incorrect. Activation of the target protein is part of the signal being ON, downstream of an already-active G protein — not the step that switches it off.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Exchanging GDP for GTP on the alpha subunit is exactly what turns the G protein ON, the reverse of the switch-off step being asked about.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Dissociation of the beta-gamma pair from alpha happens when the G protein is activated, not when it is switched off.
explanations.D: Correct. A G protein-coupled receptor activates its heterotrimeric G protein by prompting the alpha subunit to exchange bound GDP for GTP, letting alpha dissociate and activate its downstream target. Signalling switches off when the alpha subunit's own intrinsic GTPase activity hydrolyses that bound GTP back to GDP, allowing alpha to re-associate with beta-gamma and return the complex to its resting state.

questions.learning_objective: State that hydrolysis of bound GTP switches off G protein signalling.
